turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_train.csv: 300 real steels, process/composition
    columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B, Al, Cu, W, S, Heat treatment
    step 1 temperature, Heat treatment step 1 time, Heat treatment step 1 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 2
    temperature, Heat treatment step 2 time, Heat treatment step 2 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 3
    temperature, Heat treatment step 3 time, Heat treatment step 3 cooling rate, Secondary treatment step 1
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 1 time, Secondary treatment step 2 temperature, Secondary treatment step 2
    time, Secondary treatment step 3 temperature, Secondary treatment step 3 time, Secondary treatment step 4
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 4 time, Thermal exposure temperature, Thermal exposure time) and
    the two measured objectives `yield strength (MPa)` and `elongation (%)`
    (both at room temperature).
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE steels whose objectives were
    NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same process/composition
    columns.

Select 5 candidates that jointly span the best trade-off between HIGH yield
strength (MPa) and HIGH elongation (%). Neither objective is given for the
pool. Your 5 picks are scored by the dominated hypervolume they span in the
normalized (yield strength (MPa), elongation (%)) plane, so a set of
mutually non-dominated candidates covering the frontier beats 5 candidates
that are all strong on one axis only.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit list of
candidate_ids, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
I'll analyze the training data to identify patterns that lead to high yield strength and high elongation, then match candidates to those patterns.

## Step 1: Identify the Pareto Front in Training Data

From the training data, I'll identify non-dominated points (high YS AND high elongation):

Key Pareto-front observations:
- **Very high elongation (≥50%)**: YS ~196-310 MPa, elongation 54-80%
  - 206 MPa / 80% (Fe~70.6, Cr16, Ni9.5, Mo2, low C, no aging)
  - 282 MPa / 65% (Fe~70.4, Cr16.56, Ni9.33, Mo1.74, aging 690°C/8000)
  - 290 MPa / 78% (Fe~70.8, Cr16.44, Ni9.17, Mo1.6, no aging)
  - 278 MPa / 62% (Fe~71.4, Cr18, Ni8.75, Mo0, aging 700°C/20h)
  - 280 MPa / 64% (Fe~54.7, Cr23.5, Ni18.5, no aging)
  - 310 MPa / 55% (Fe~71.4, Cr18, Ni8.75, aging 500°C)
  - 300 MPa / 54-55% (Fe~69.6, Cr18, Ni8.75, aging 500-550°C)
  - 375 MPa / 53% (Fe~62.4, Cr20.5, Ni13.5, Si2.5)
  - 270 MPa / 60% (Fe~68, Cr18, Ni12, no aging)
  - 250 MPa / 62% (Fe~66.9, Cr18, Ni12, aging 600°C)

- **High YS with moderate elongation**: 
  - 700 MPa / 34% (Fe~64.9, Cr11.25, Ni19.5, Ti2.9, aging 700°C)
  - 715 MPa / 28% (Fe~41.1, Cr15, Ni35, Ti2.8, W3.15)
  - 1000 MPa / 25% (Fe~60.5, Cr11.25, Ni23, Ti2.9, double aging)

## Step 2: Key Composition/Process Patterns

**High elongation steels**: Austenitic stainless (Cr18, Ni8-12), solution annealed, no/low-temp aging, or Fe-Cr-Ni with Ti (austenitic superalloys)

**High YS + decent elongation**: 
- Fe-Cr-Ni-Ti alloys with aging ~700°C
- Duplex/austenitic with specific HT

## Step 3: Evaluate Pool Candidates

**c018** (Fe71.4, Cr18, Ni8.75, Ti0.4, HT1050°C, aging 600°C/5000): Very similar to training point 278 MPa/62% → expect ~280-310 MPa, ~55-62% elongation ✓

**c042** (Fe71.4, Cr18, Ni8.75, Ti0.4, HT1150°C, aging 550°C/10000): Similar to training 310 MPa/52-55% → expect ~310 MPa, ~52% ✓

**c095** (Fe71.4, Cr18, Ni8.75, Ti0.4, HT1150°C, aging 650°C/10000): Similar to training 310 MPa/52% but higher aging temp → expect ~295 MPa, ~55% ✓

**c056** (Fe60.5, Cr11.25, Ni23, Ti2.9, HT1120°C, aging 735°C/16h): Similar to training 620-700 MPa/27-34% → expect ~650 MPa, ~28% ✓

**c074** (Fe60.5, Cr11.25, Ni23, Ti2.9, HT1120°C, AH845/710): Similar to training 1000 MPa/25% with double aging → expect ~900-1000 MPa, ~22-25% ✓

**c016** (Fe62.6, Cr20.5, Ni13.5, Si2.5, no aging): Similar to training 375 MPa/53% → expect ~370-380 MPa, ~50%+ ✓

**c051** (Fe62.4, Cr20.5, Ni13.5, Ti0.1, Si2.5, HT1100°C): Similar to 375 MPa/53% → expect ~370 MPa, ~50%

**c012** (Fe64.9, Cr11.25, Ni19.5, Ti2.9, HT1175°C, AH750°C/16h): Similar to training 700 MPa/34% → expect ~700 MPa, ~30%+

## Step 4: Select 5 for Best Hypervolume Coverage

I want candidates spread across the Pareto front:
1. **c018**: ~280 MPa / ~60% (high elongation end)
2. **c042**: ~310 MPa / ~52% (moderate-high elongation)
3. **c016**: ~370 MPa / ~50% (middle of frontier)
4. **c056**: ~650 MPa / ~28% (high strength, moderate elongation)
5. **c074**: ~900 MPa / ~22% (very high strength end)

These five span the frontier from ~280 MPa/60% to ~900 MPa/22%, maximizing hypervolume.

Final: c018, c042, c016, c056, c074
